lines.trans: I have a business proposal for you.
A boy named Alexei attends your kindergarten.
Are you blackmailing me right now?
I agree, but life can be cruel.
In the evening the boy will tell all at home.
I hope he will like everything.

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.

бывать.gloss: to happen, to be (sometimes); to visit

meanings.en: to happen, to exist, there can be
meanings.note: 3rd person бывает = there is / can be
Часто бывать где-то. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to happen, to be (sometimes); to visit', paired with 'быть'.

examples.text: У мужчины бывает не только жена.
examples.trans: A man can have more than just a wife.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
E.g. a school evening. Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

дойти.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Takes до + genitive. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to reach, walk as far as', paired with 'доходить'.
Reach the recipient. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to reach, walk as far as', paired with 'доходить'.

examples.text: Но они, к сожалению, не дошли до вас.
examples.trans: But unfortunately, it never reached you.
We quickly walked as far as the house.
Crawl forward! We have almost arrived.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Location; compare домой = homeward. Core Russian adv meaning 'at home' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The main thing is, you keep him at home.

examples.text: А Осипенко сейчас дома лежит. У него больное сердце.
examples.trans: And Osipenko is lying at home right now. He has a sick heart.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.en: cruel, harsh, ruthless (short form: жесток / жестока / жестоки)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cruel, harsh, severe').

examples.text: Анатолий Иванович, вы были слишком жестоки.
examples.trans: Anatoly Ivanovich, you were too harsh.
I agree, but life can be cruel.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
А именно = namely. Core Russian part meaning 'exactly, namely, precisely' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'otherwise' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'otherwise' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Go, or else you'll be late.

examples.text: Пятьдесят метров, не больше. Иначе будет сигнал.
examples.trans: Fifty metres, no more. Otherwise there'll be a signal.

meanings.note: Predicative: очень интересно. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Как интересно!. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: чувствовать себя комфортно = to feel comfortable

examples.text: В новой квартире нам живётся очень комфортно.
examples.trans: We live very comfortably in the new flat.

meanings.note: A male child. Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'boy' in everyday Russian.
used to address a child you don't know

Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'конец').

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

meanings.note: Большие неприятности = big trouble. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'приятность'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'trouble, nuisance, unpleasantness' in everyday Russian.
Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
For masculine and neuter things. Core Russian pron meaning 'he; it' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought
meanings.note: Once, for a while. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (it over)', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.en: to be liked, to make a good impression
meanings.note: Person who likes is in the dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нравиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be liked, to please', paired with 'нравиться'.

examples.text: Синеозерск понравился в Москве больше других мест.
examples.trans: In Moscow they liked Sineozersk more than other places.
Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

meanings.note: у меня есть предложение = I have an offer

In grammar. Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'offer, proposal; sentence' in everyday Russian.

Сделать предложение. Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'offer, proposal; sentence' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It's a good offer, of course.

examples.text: Значит, предложение такое. Ты мне говоришь, где твои сорок миллионов.
examples.trans: So, here's the offer. You tell me where your forty million is.

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: about something: рассказать о + prepositional
ironic: Сталину расскажите = tell that to Stalin

Colloquial for детский сад. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'адик'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'daycare, kindergarten' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Дочь хочу к вам в садик записать.
examples.trans: I want to enroll my daughter in your daycare.

examples.text: Утром родители ведут детей в садик.
examples.trans: In the morning parents take children to kindergarten.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

'Слушаю' = I'm listening. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.
